issue.title: Scope show_empty()'s detail-header summary cache clear to the deselected agent, not the whole cache
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-l6.6 (land phase of epic sase-l6, SASE CONTEXT incremental enrichment); named as follow-up 3 in plans:202608/sase_context_incremental.md.

show_empty() (src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/prompt_panel/_agent_display_render.py:494) clears the whole detail-header summary cache wholesale on deselection. Before epic sase-l6, that cache held one monolithic DetailHeaderSummary per agent; after phases sase-l6.3/sase-l6.4 (per-lane resolution, caching, and streaming), it holds independently-resolved, independently-cached lanes (DetailContextLane) that are comparatively expensive to rebuild (store-backed lanes in particular). Throwing away every agent's cached lanes on any deselection means re-selecting a previously-viewed agent pays the full lane-resolution cost again even though the per-lane freshness machinery from sase-l6.3 would otherwise have kept it warm.

Scope: evaluate whether show_empty() can scope its cache clear to the specific agent being deselected (or drop the clear entirely, relying on per-lane staleness/generation checks from sase-l6.3 to keep a stale cache from rendering), rather than dropping every agent's resolved lanes.

payload.entry: Triage sweep 2026-08-14 (requested by the project owner: keep the seven highest-impact open tasks, close the rest). All six are sase-l6 land-phase follow-ups on a path the epic already fixed with process-wide revalidating snapshot caches: store pruning/rotation, moving the artifact-file index into Rust indexed storage, scoping show_empty()'s cache clear, cold-cache re-measurement, auditing non-TUI read_artifact_file_index callers, and one bench budget (bench_tui_jk selected-tribe fold level 1, ~48 ms vs a 40 ms p95 budget on a 64-core host at loadavg ~30). No independent reporters, no user-visible defect. The one resolver kept open from this cluster is sase-lw, which measured 400-800 ms per TUI selection with no cache at all. Store growth stays visible: ~/.sase/artifacts/index.jsonl is 7.8 MB today -- re-file with a +1 and a fresh figure if it starts costing real latency.

payload.close_reason: Deprioritized in the 2026-08-14 task-backlog triage: epic sase-l6 already landed the SASE CONTEXT enrichment win these follow-ups refine.
